title: An ample invertible module over an affine base: a power is the pullback of O(1) along an immersion into projective space
statement: Let $A$ be a ring, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] which is ample on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. For $n\ge0$ let $P_n=\operatorname{Proj}(A[x_0,\dots,x_n])$ [def-pc-proj] ($\deg x_k=1$), with structure morphism $q_n:P_n\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ (on each standard open $D_+(x_k)=\operatorname{Spec}(A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_{(x_k)})$ it is induced by the ring map $A\to A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_{(x_k)}$), and let $\mathcal O_{P_n}(1)$ be the twisting module of [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Then there exist integers $d\ge1$ and $n\ge0$, an immersion $i:X\to P_n$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] (a closed immersion into an open subscheme $U\subseteq P_n$ followed by the inclusion $U\to P_n$ [def-weil-open-immersion]) with $q_n\circ i=f$, and an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}\cong i^*\mathcal O_{P_n}(1)$, where $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ is the $d$-fold tensor power [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and $i^*$ is the pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01VS (morphisms-lemma-quasi-projective-finite-type-over-S) for S = Spec(A); equivalently Lemma 01VT (morphisms-lemma-finite-type-over-affine-ample-very-ample), implication (1) => (5), as used in the proof of Cohomology of Schemes Lemma 0B5T; P^n_{Spec A} (Constructions, Definition 01NF, constructions-definition-projective-space) is identified with Proj(A[T_0,...,T_n]) by Constructions Lemma 01O3 (constructions-lemma-relative-proj-base-change)

proof.text:
*A finite cover by affine loci of sections of one power of $\mathcal L$.* For $n\ge1$ and $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$ let $X_s$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. By condition (1) of that definition $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and by [lem-weil-pbc-ample-scheme-separated] $X$ is separated, i.e. separated over the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. By condition (2) every $x\in X$ lies in an affine open $X_s$ with $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, $n\ge1$; these opens cover $X$, so finitely many do: $X=X_{c_0}\cup\dots\cup X_{c_r}$ with $X_{c_k}$ affine, $c_k\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n_k})$, $n_k\ge1$. (If $X=\emptyset$, take $d=1$, $n=0$ and for $i$ the empty morphism, which is a closed immersion into the empty open subscheme of $P_0$; the isomorphism $\mathcal L\cong i^*\mathcal O_{P_0}(1)$ is between zero modules. From now on $X
eq\emptyset$, so $r\ge0$.) Put $m=n_0n_1\cdots n_r\ge1$ and $a_k=c_k^{\otimes m/n_k}\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$, using the canonical isomorphisms $\mathcal L^{\otimes p}\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes q}\cong\mathcal L^{\otimes p+q}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $X_{a_k}=X_{c_k}$: at $x\in X$ choose a generator $\epsilon$ of the free rank-one $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $(\mathcal L^{\otimes n_k})_x$ [def-sc-invertible-module], write $(c_k)_x=u\epsilon$; then $(a_k)_x=u^{m/n_k}\epsilon^{\otimes m/n_k}$ with $\epsilon^{\otimes m/n_k}$ a generator of $(\mathcal L^{\otimes m})_x$, and $u^{m/n_k}
otin\mathfrak m_x$ iff $u
otin\mathfrak m_x$ since $\mathfrak m_x$ is prime. The same computation shows $X_{a^{\otimes e}}=X_a$ for every section $a$ of a power of $\mathcal L$ and $e\ge1$. So $X=X_{a_0}\cup\dots\cup X_{a_r}$ with every $X_{a_k}$ affine and every $a_k\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$. (Stacks 01VS takes the $X_a$ from the basis of Properties 01Q3 and needs each $X_{a_i}$ to map into an affine open of $S$; here $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine, so a finite cover, which the definition gives directly, suffices.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01VS (lemma-quasi-projective-finite-type-over-S), proof, first paragraph: the finitely many a_0,...,a_n in A_+ with X = union of the affine X_{a_i}; Properties, Definition 01PS (definition-ample)

proof.text: *The affine pieces are finitely generated $A$-algebras.* Since $f$ is locally of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] applied to the affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, whose ring of sections is $A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and to the affine open $U=X_{a_k}$ (trivially $f(U)\subseteq V$) shows that the ring map $A\to\mathcal O_X(X_{a_k})$ induced by $f$ (that is, $f^\sharp$ followed by restriction) is of finite type. Choose, for each $k=0,\dots,r$, finitely many elements $f_{k1},\dots,f_{kn_k}\in\mathcal O_X(X_{a_k})$ ($n_k\ge0$) generating $\mathcal O_X(X_{a_k})$ as an $A$-algebra.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01VS, proof, first paragraph ('By Lemma 01T2 we see that the ring maps O_S(V_i) -> O_X(X_{a_i}) are of finite type')

proof.text: *The generators as quotients of global sections of one power $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$.* Fix $k$ and $l\in\{1,\dots,n_k\}$. The module $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ is invertible (locally $\mathcal L\cong\mathcal O_X$, so locally $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}\cong\mathcal O_X$ [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), $X_{a_k}$ is the complement of the zero locus of $a_k$, and $X$ is quasi-compact and separated over an affine scheme (Step 1). So [lem-pc-section-clearing-denominators], applied to $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$, its section $a_k$, the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal O_X$ and $t=f_{kl}\in\Gamma(X_{a_k},\mathcal O_X)$, gives $e_{kl}\ge0$ and $u_{kl}\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X\otimes(\mathcal L^{\otimes m})^{\otimes e_{kl}})=\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes me_{kl}})$ with $u_{kl}|_{X_{a_k}}=f_{kl}\,a_k^{\otimes e_{kl}}|_{X_{a_k}}$ (identifying $\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathcal N=\mathcal N$ and $(\mathcal L^{\otimes m})^{\otimes e}=\mathcal L^{\otimes me}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; for $e_{kl}=0$, $u_{kl}\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$). Let $E=1+\max_{k,l}e_{kl}$ ($E=1$ if there are no $f_{kl}$) and $d=mE\ge1$. Put $b_k=a_k^{\otimes E}\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$ and $b_{kl}=u_{kl}\otimes a_k^{\otimes(E-e_{kl})}\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$ (here $E-e_{kl}\ge1$). Then $X_{b_k}=X_{a_k}$ (Step 1) and $b_{kl}|_{X_{b_k}}=f_{kl}\,a_k^{\otimes e_{kl}}\otimes a_k^{\otimes(E-e_{kl})}|_{X_{b_k}}=f_{kl}\,b_k|_{X_{b_k}}$. These are the sections $a_i^{N/\deg a_i}$, $a_{ij}a_i^{N/\deg(a_i)-e_{ij}}$ of the source with $N=d$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01VS, proof, first paragraph (write f_{ij} = a_{ij}/a_i^{e_{ij}} by Properties Lemma 01PW, label properties-lemma-invert-s-sections; N a common multiple of the degrees)

proof.text: *The morphism $j$ to $P_n$.* Index the $1+r+\sum_kn_k$ sections $b_k$ ($0\le k\le r$) and $b_{kl}$ ($0\le k\le r$, $1\le l\le n_k$) of $\mathcal M:=\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ by $\{0,\dots,n\}$, $n=r+\sum_kn_k$, the section $b_k$ getting the index $k$ and $b_{kl}$ an index $(kl)>r$; write the variables of $A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ accordingly as $x_k$, $x_{(kl)}$. $\mathcal M$ is invertible (Step 3) and $X=X_{b_0}\cup\dots\cup X_{b_r}$ (Steps 1 and 3), so the loci of all $n+1$ sections cover $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sections-morphism-to-proj-polynomial-ring] (with $Y=X$, $g=f$, $m=n$) there are a morphism $j:X\to P_n$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:j^*\mathcal O_{P_n}(1)\to\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ with: $q_n\circ j=f$; $j^{-1}(D_+(x_k))=X_{b_k}=X_{a_k}$ for $0\le k\le r$; and for $0\le k\le r$ the ring map $\theta_k:A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_{(x_k)}\to\mathcal O_X(X_{a_k})$ induced by $j$ is an $A$-algebra homomorphism (for the $A$-algebra structure through $f^\sharp$, the one of Step 2) with $\theta_k(x_{(kl)}/x_k)=b_{kl}/b_k$. By the uniqueness of $b_{kl}/b_k$ in that statement and $b_{kl}|_{X_{b_k}}=f_{kl}\,b_k|_{X_{b_k}}$ (Step 3), $b_{kl}/b_k=f_{kl}$, so $\theta_k(x_{(kl)}/x_k)=f_{kl}$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01VS, proof, first paragraph ('Hence they give rise to a morphism j : X -> P^m_S ... j^*O(1) = L^{otimes N} ... j^{-1}(D_+(T_i)) = X_{a_i} ... pulling back T_{ij}/T_i via j^sharp we get f_{ij}'), via Constructions Lemma 01NE and Definition 01NF

proof.text: *$j$ is an immersion.* Let $U=D_+(x_0)\cup\dots\cup D_+(x_r)\subseteq P_n$, an open subset, viewed as an open subscheme with inclusion $\iota:U\to P_n$, an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. By Step 4, $j^{-1}(U)=X_{a_0}\cup\dots\cup X_{a_r}=X$, so $j(X)\subseteq U$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] there is a unique $j':X\to U$ with $\iota\circ j'=j$. We show that $j'$ is a closed immersion using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] (2) for the covering of $U$ by $V_k=D_+(x_k)$, $0\le k\le r$: each $V_k$ is affine, $V_k=\operatorname{Spec}(A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_{(x_k)})$ [def-pc-proj]; $j'^{-1}(V_k)=j^{-1}(V_k)=X_{a_k}$ is affine (Step 1); and since $\iota$ is the identity on $V_k\subseteq U$, the ring map $j'^\sharp_{V_k}$ is $\theta_k$. Its image is an $A$-subalgebra of $\mathcal O_X(X_{a_k})$ (as $\theta_k$ is an $A$-algebra map) containing $f_{k1},\dots,f_{kn_k}$ (Step 4), which generate $\mathcal O_X(X_{a_k})$ as an $A$-algebra for the same $A$-algebra structure (Step 2); so $\theta_k$ is surjective. Hence $j'$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $i:=j=\iota\circ j'$ is a closed immersion into the open subscheme $U$ followed by the inclusion $U\to P_n$, i.e. an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01VS, proof, first paragraph ('Hence the morphism j restricted to X_{a_i} gives a closed immersion of X_{a_i} into the affine open D_+(T_i) ... Hence we conclude that the morphism j is an immersion')

proof.text: *Conclusion.* With $d\ge1$ (Step 3), $n\ge0$ and the immersion $i=j:X\to P_n$ (Step 5) we have $q_n\circ i=f$ and the isomorphism $\alpha^{-1}:\mathcal L^{\otimes d}\to i^*\mathcal O_{P_n}(1)$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules (Step 4).
